answer: A yarrow garden guards an agent economy with Padovan loom-weaving: every new identity must weave one cloth of yarrow-dyed thread on a single loom, and the stitch count follows the Padovan pattern, so the first fake weaves 1 stitch, the second 1, the third 2, the tenth 12 and the twentieth 200, and twenty fakes together weave 813 stitches. Bulk farming fails because one weaver holds one thread and each cloth must be finished before the next is warped, so no stitch can be woven in parallel or bought; like a gardener tending one bed at a time, never in bulk.
